# Circuitoon

> Circuit diagrams AI agents can design, check and hand you: pictorial wiring sheets of real parts, laid out from a JSON netlist and verified pin by pin.

An agent writes a `circuitoon-netlist/1` file naming built-in parts and nets as `REF.PIN`. The `circuitoon` CLI lays it out on breadboards with wires, checks the sheet against the netlist and against a wiring checker (shorts, reversed polarity, wrong supply voltage, pin rules, I2C addresses, USB cables, roles and current), renders PNG and SVG, writes a bill of materials and a KiCad netlist, and makes a link that opens the sheet in the browser editor at https://mbarc.github.io/circuitoon/. The sheet travels in the link's fragment, so nothing is uploaded.

It is a good fit for hookup pictures of maker projects: ESP32, Arduino Nano or Raspberry Pi Pico boards with sensors, displays, batteries, switches and LEDs, and Raspberry Pis, computers and USB hubs joined by USB cables. It does not do PCB layout (it hands the design to KiCad as a netlist instead), symbolic schematics or circuit simulation. There are 173 built-in parts. A part that isn't built in can be made with `circuitoon module new` from a short spec (name, category, pins per side in physical order, sourced from the maker's datasheet); `module check` lints it and `module render` draws it. Such parts are reported as custom and unverified. People make parts in the editor's part maker (New part) the same way.

Install in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add MBarc/circuitoon` then `/plugin install circuitoon@circuitoon`. Without Claude Code, clone the repo and run `node plugin/bin/circuitoon.mjs --help` (Node 22 or newer, no npm install; Chrome or Edge for PNG). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 findings that block, 2 invalid input, 3 environment problem or internal error.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/README.md): what it does, when to use it, install, the command list, exit codes, and what is and isn't verified.
- [circuitoon-design skill](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/SKILL.md): the full agent workflow, the rules for presenting a sheet, and how to read the gate.
- [Netlist format](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/netlist-format.md): every field of `circuitoon-netlist/1`, repeats, net labels and the `--keep` partial format.
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/cli.md): commands, flags, exit codes, gate outputs and the bill of materials.

## Schemas

- [JSON schemas](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/tree/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/schemas): every command's `--json` output, one file each, plus the error document.
- [Error schema](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/schemas/error.schema.json): what a failed command prints under `--json`.
- [Gate schema](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/schemas/gate.schema.json): `gate.json`, with `ok`, `ready`, artifact hashes and the "not checked" list.

## Optional

- [Embedded parts](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/module-schema.md): how to add a part that isn't built in, from its maker's documentation.
- [Custom part skill](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-custom-part/SKILL.md): making a part with `module new`, sourcing and checking its pinout, rendering it and using it in a netlist.
- [Part spec schema](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/schemas/part-spec.schema.json): the input of `module new`.
- [Worked examples](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/plugin/skills/circuitoon-design/references/examples.md): five netlists that pass the gate, from one LED to a design split across four sheets.
- [Product plan](https://github.com/MBarc/circuitoon/blob/main/docs/PRD.md): the formats, the checker's rules and the roadmap.
